description: Change of use from dwelling house (Class C3) to a HMO - house in multiple occupation (Sui Generis), involving two-storey side extension, part single, part two-storey rear extension, rear dormer and front rooflights.
decision_conditions: The development hereby permitted must be begun not later than the end of three years from the date of this permission. Reason: To comply with the provisions of S.51 of the Planning & Compulsory Purchase Act 2004.

The development hereby permitted shall be carried out in accordance with the following approved plans:Location Plan Dated 12 Jun 2026Existing and Proposed Block Plan, Location Plan 25_1013_300A Rev A Dated 08.06.2026Existing Ground Floor Plan and Existing First Floor Plan 25_1013_301A Rev A Dated 08.06.2026	Existing Roof Plan 25_1013_302A Rev A Dated 08.06.2026	Existing Front Elevation and Existing Rear Elevation 25_1013_303A Rev A Dated 08.06.2026Existing Side Elevation and Existing Cross Section AA 25_1013_304A Rev A Dated 08.06.2026 Proposed Ground Floor Plan and Proposed First Floor Plan 25_1013_305A Rev A Dated 08.06.2026 Proposed Loft Floor Plan and Proposed Roof Plan	25_1013_306A Rev A	 Dated 08.06.2026Proposed Front Elevation and Proposed Rear Elevation 25_1013_307A Rev A Dated 08.06.2026Proposed Side Elevation and Proposed Cross Section AA	25_1013_308A Rev A Dated 08.06.2026Proposed Sustainable Drainage 25_1013_309A Rev A Dated 08.06.2026Flood Risk Assessment ref. U0855 FRA-v1 Dated June 26 SuDS Maintenance Plan Dated 12 Jun 2026Covering Letter Dated 12 Jun 2026Planning Statement Dated January 2026Highway Safety Impact FormSuDS Pro FormaReason: For the avoidance of doubt and in the interests of proper planning.

The development hereby permitted shall not be occupied by more than NINE residents at any one time. Reason: To ensure that the future occupation of the building does not adversely affect the adjoining premises/immediate.

No independent cooking or laundry facilities shall be installed in any of the respective bedrooms and the communal kitchen and dining/living rooms shall be retained in perpetuity. Reason: To accord with the stipulations of definition as a House of Multiple Occupation and to safeguard the residential character of the surrounding area.

Prior to occupation; unless otherwise agreed; cycle parking shall be provided in compliance with the following criteria:i) Provision of a minimum of NINE long stay cycle parking spaces and TWO short stay spaces.ii) In an accessible location; the access route to each long stay store should be a minimum of 1.2m wide to enable the bike to enter the store, should be step free and involve no more than 2 doors or gates [excluding the store door] which must also have a minimum opening width of 1.2m.iii) Secured with a British Standard mortice lock or access fob.iv) Fully enclosed: 4 walls and a roof.Such facilities to be retained permanently thereafter.Reason: To ensure the provision and availability of adequate cycle parking.

Notwithstanding the approved plans, prior to first occupation of the development hereby permitted, details of the design and siting of refuse storage facilities including facilities for the recycling of waste to satisfy the future number of occupiers on site, shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority, in accordance with the Household Recycling and Waste Planning Guidance for New Developments (2024). Once approved the development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved details prior to first occupation and retained for the lifetime of the development. Reason: In order to facilitate efficient, safe and clean removal of household refuse, the location and accessibility of refuse storage plus to maintain safety on the Highway.

All new external work shall be carried out in materials that resemble, as closely as possible, in colour and texture as specified in the approved application.  Reason: To safeguard the appearance of the premises and the character of the immediate area.

The development shall not commence until details of source control Sustainable Drainage Systems (SuDS) have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. Source control SuDS measures may include green roofs, rain gardens, permeable paving or other appropriate measures. The submitted details shall include plans, specifications, calculations where necessary, and maintenance information. The development shall thereafter be carried out and maintained in accordance with the approved details.Reason: To ensure the sustainable management of surface water, minimise flood risk, minimise the discharge of surface water outside the curtilage of the property, and ensure that the drainage system remains functional for the lifetime of the development, in accordance with Core Strategy Policy CP28, Development Management Document Policy DMD 61, London Plan Policies SI 12 and SI 13, and the National Planning Policy Framework.
